findings.reason: One bad historical record aborts `log` and every `roster`, goal-named views, instead of degrading a row; incorrect behavior.
`roster --live` (B8) presents stale threads state as live when the read is failing; a misleading result in a goal-named path.
Repeated per-clone history walks and an ignored injected cap are a cost and structure issue; the staleness output stays correct.
The goal names `ops` filters (B3), and no test through the CLI shows `--seat` or `--teamspace` filtering; this is a missing test for a goal-named behavior.
Unmeasured performance cost in the last_change pass, bounded by the scan cap; it does not change correctness.
Revwalk sort cost is an unmeasured performance concern and does not change results.
`log --since` can silently drop in-window commits when commit times are non-monotonic and still reports a complete scan; incorrect result in goal-named `log`.
`roster --live` exits 1 instead of 6 on an integrity failure; this breaks the goal's unchanged-behavior exit-6 rule for a goal-named view.
`instructions stack` (B2) fails the whole command on a history lookup error that should only null the `changed` column; incorrect behavior in a goal-named view.
The test for the `roster --live` adds-no-commit behavior can fail falsely and blame the wrong cause, so it does not reliably cover a goal-named behavior.
Design-doc staleness is documentation hygiene; the goal names no doc update.
Row-shape consistency between `ops --json` and `log --json` is an API-polish improvement; `ops --json` still works and the spec leaves the row shape undefined.
`kind_word` in `log.rs` outputs 'nativesession' instead of 'native_session' in the `log` row `kind` field, a wrong value in a goal-named view, beyond the duplicated-helper cleanup.
